messages:
Grace Kim: seeing something weird on INT8 runs in perf-lab. Auto-selector is picking FP16 GEMM for a set of decode shapes even though INT8 weights are loaded + `quant_mode=int8` in config. This is showing up as a ~12-18% throughput hit vs last week.

Grace Kim: from the logs (added by my local patch):
```
quant_mode=int8
op=gemm
shape: M=256 N=11008 K=4096  (decode)
selected_kernel=gemm_fp16_tc
reason=best_estimated_latency
```
Expected `gemm_int8_w8a8`.

Noah Patel: ^ that’s bad. is the selector basing on alignment / tile constraints? M=256/N=11008/K=4096 should be fine for int8 tc paths on H100.

Yuki Sato: can you paste the exact runtime version + flags? also which model family? (llama vs qwen vs mistral)

Grace Kim: model is `qwen2.5-7b-instruct` (hosted preset). runtime commit `9f2d0b1` from today’s perf build. flags:
- `RWD_QUANT_MODE=int8`
- `RWD_KERNEL_AUTOPICK=1`
- `RWD_INT8_ALLOW_FALLBACK=1` (default)

Grace Kim: repro is consistent on H100 + H200; A100 seems to pick int8 correctly.

Isabella Rossi: I can repro with a microbench too. This is the smallest snippet I found:
```
# H100 SXM, cuda 12.4
./bin/microbench_gemm \
  --dtype_a=int8 --dtype_w=int8 --accum=fp16 \
  --m=256 --n=11008 --k=4096 \
  --warmup=50 --iters=200 \
  --autoselect=1 --print_selected=1

# output:
# selected: gemm_fp16_tc
# candidate int8 rejected: kTileConstraintMismatch
```
So selector thinks it violates a constraint (?) but the int8 kernel runs fine when forced.

Rina Kobayashi: for the end-to-end harness I can get the same by pinning to streaming chat preset + concurrency 16. command:
```
bench run e2e_chat_streaming \
  --config configs/top_hosted/qwen2.5_7b_int8_h100.json \
  --params decode.max_new_tokens=256 \
  --params scheduler.max_batch_tokens=8192
```
Artifacts: `s3://redwood-perf/bench/2024-10-30/qwen-int8-autopick-fp16/`

Marcus Reed: does this only happen in decode? I wonder if we’re tagging phase incorrectly and selector is using prefill constraints.

Grace Kim: only decode. prefill is selecting INT8 attention + GEMM correctly. the mismatch is specifically on these “mid-sized” M shapes. when M is smaller (64/128) it still picks int8. when M is bigger (512+) it also picks int8. super odd.

Yuki Sato: I pulled the selector code. there’s a path where we “round” K to nearest multiple for cache keys, but then validate constraints against the rounded value instead of the real K. if the rounded K triggers a conservative constraint check it could reject the int8 kernel.

Yuki Sato: can you confirm if the kernel registry entry has something like `kMultipleOf=256` and we’re rounding K up?

Isabella Rossi: yep. dumping the candidates:
```
int8_candidate: requires K % 256 == 0
reported_K=4352 (rounded)
actual_K=4096
=> reject
```
So we’re literally rounding 4096 -> 4352 for the selector check. :facepalm:

Noah Patel: that explains why A100 behaves differently if it has a different rounded key / candidate list.

Grace Kim: wow ok. so it’s a selector bug, not kernel perf.

Yuki Sato: I’ll put up a PR to:
1) use actual M/N/K for constraint validation
2) keep rounded dims only for cache key / heuristic bucket
3) add a unit test covering `K=4096` and the qwen projection N=11008 shapes

Yuki Sato: PR will reference this thread + add reproduction case.

Connor O'Brien: please tag it release-blocking if it impacts hosted presets. if we’re silently falling back to fp16 we’ll get perf regressions without any obvious alerts.

Rina Kobayashi: +1, also can we emit a warning event when `quant_mode=int8` but selected kernel family != int8? would help perf canary.

Noah Patel: we already have a tracing span PR in flight for kernel selection logging (I think 10621?). but a cheap counter/structured log on fallback would be good too.

Yuki Sato: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/10625
- fix selector rounding bug
- add unit test `test_int8_autopick_does_not_reject_due_to_rounded_k`
- add debug log `kernel_autoselect_fallback` behind `RWD_PERF_LOGS=1`

Grace Kim: pulled 10625 locally, reran microbench + e2e. now selects `gemm_int8_w8a8_tc` and throughput is back.

Grace Kim: numbers (H100):
- before (fp16 fallback): 6.9k tok/s
- after (int8): 8.0k tok/s
p95 TPOT improved ~11%.

Marcus Reed: nice. can we add this shape to the scheduler experiment matrix too? tail latency on mixed workloads was where we first noticed.

Rina Kobayashi: I’ll add a harness assertion in the quant suite: fail if `quant_mode=int8` and >5% of decode GEMMs are fp16-selected (unless allowlisted). will open a separate task.

buildkite-bot: Build #118233 passed for redwood/redwood PR #10625 (unit-tests, lint, gpu-smoke-h100).

Connor O'Brien: merging once Grace signs off. please also drop a note in release train thread with the risk assessment (should be low-risk, selector-only).

Yuki Sato: merged. will backport if needed for this week’s runtime release. thanks all.

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: signing off. adding the before/after artifacts link to ENG-24814 too so we don’t lose context.
